D-001.threat: Process resource exhaustion — attacker exhausts process resources causing denial of service
D-001.cause: No resource limits or rate limiting — process allocates unbounded resources in response to requests
D-001.attack: Attacker sends high volume of requests consuming all available CPU, memory, or file handles

D-002.threat: Process crash via malformed input — attacker crashes the process with crafted input
D-002.cause: Insufficient input validation — malformed input causes buffer overflow or unhandled exception
D-002.attack: Attacker sends crafted input that triggers a crash, causing the process to become unavailable

D-003.threat: Data flow disruption — attacker blocks or delays the data flow
D-003.cause: No redundancy or timeout protection — disruption causes loss of communication
D-003.attack: Attacker blocks or corrupts the data flow causing dependent components to lose communication

D-004.threat: Data store unavailability — attacker makes the data store inaccessible
D-004.cause: No redundancy for data store access — single point of failure
D-004.attack: Attacker fills the data store to capacity or corrupts its index causing all operations to fail

D-005.threat: Data store deletion attack — attacker deletes critical stored data
D-005.cause: Data store lacks access control or backup — critical data can be deleted and is unrecoverable
D-005.attack: Attacker gains write access and deletes critical configuration or state data causing system failure

D-006.threat: System denial of service — attacker renders the system unavailable
D-006.cause: No rate limiting at system boundary — the system processes all incoming requests without restriction
D-006.attack: Attacker floods the system with requests preventing legitimate users from accessing services

D-007.threat: Multiprocess service exhaustion — attacker drives a multiprocess component to unavailability
D-007.cause: No resource quotas or rate limiting across the component's processes — aggregate load is unbounded
D-007.attack: Attacker sustains high request volume until the multiprocess component exhausts CPU, memory, or worker capacity and stops serving
